# Spotify API fixtures

Recorded and documented Spotify Web API responses for tests. They are plain JSON with no dependency on MSW or Jest, so handlers, fixture builders or any other tooling can load them. They live under `src/` because Create React App's Jest only looks there and the app's TypeScript can import JSON from there.

Each fixture file has the same shape:

```json
{ "method": "GET", "url": "https://api.spotify.com/v1/me", "status": 200, "headers": {}, "body": {} }
```

## Layout

- `live/`: responses recorded on 2026-10-17 from a dedicated Spotify test account, then scrubbed and trimmed. Generated by the scrub script; don't edit by hand. `live/index.json` lists every file with its URL and any trimming applied.
- `documented/`: responses that couldn't be recorded live (token endpoint, 401, 429, 5xx), written from Spotify's documentation. `documented/index.json` links each one to its source.
- `private-value-hashes.json`: SHA-256 hashes of the values the scrub script replaced. Never store the values themselves.
- `scrub.ts`: the scrub and leak-check logic; `scrub.test.ts` covers it.
- `leaks.test.ts`: fails if any file in this directory contains a hashed private value or something shaped like a Spotify access or refresh token.
- `builders.ts`: fixture builders (`buildTrack`, `buildPlaylist`, `buildPlaylistItem`, `buildLocalTrack`, `buildPage`, `paginate`, `pageAt`, `apiError` and friends). Each starts from a live response and takes overrides, deriving `href`, `uri` and `external_urls` from the `id`, so a test states only the values it asserts on. Like the JSON, they don't depend on MSW or Jest; `src/mocks/handlers.ts` wraps them in MSW handlers.

## Regenerating `live/`

Log in to the app at http://127.0.0.1:3000 as the test account and use it (playlist list, Liked Songs, Export All with every optional column), noting each Spotify GET URL it requests. Then replay those URLs in the page with the same read-only token, saving each response as `{ url, status, headers, body }` in one JSON array. agent-browser's HAR recordings have no response bodies, which is why the URLs are replayed. Keep the capture and any HAR files outside the repo: they carry bearer tokens. Then run:

```sh
mise run fixtures:scrub /path/to/responses-raw.json
mise test
```

The script rewrites `live/` and merges the new private value hashes into `private-value-hashes.json`, keeping old ones so earlier captures stay checked.

## What the scrub does

- Reads the account's user ID, display name and `account_id` from the `/me` response, and the playlists it owns from the playlist list responses, then replaces those values everywhere they appear (URLs, `href`, `uri`, `external_urls`, owner and `added_by` objects) with stable fakes: `exportifytestuser`, `Test User`, `FakeAcct00`, `fakeplaylist0000000001`… and `fakesnapshot…0001`….
- Leaves public catalogue data alone: tracks, artists, albums, shows, and playlists owned by Spotify or other users, including their IDs, snapshot IDs and images.
- Cuts every `available_markets` array to two countries, which was most of the 23 MB capture.
- Trims playlist pages longer than 25 items to their first 25, keeping the real `total`, `limit`, `offset` and `next`. A test that pages through those playlists will see fewer items than `total` says.
- Keeps the first `/albums`, `/artists` and `/audio-features` batch, plus any batch with `null` entries, and drops the rest.
- Drops `content-length`, which no longer matches the trimmed body.

## Real-world details worth knowing

- `/me` now includes `account_id`. With the app's scopes it has no `email`, `country` or `product`.
- Playlist objects carry both `tracks` and a newer `items` link (`{ href, total }`), and playlist entries carry both `track` and a duplicate `item`, plus `video_thumbnail`.
- With extended quota, Spotify still returns `popularity`, `available_markets` and `preview_url`.
- "Indie Mix ✨ Ümlauts & Émojis 🎸" contains a podcast episode (`type: "episode"` but `episode: false, track: true`, with the show in `album` and `artists`), a duplicate track, multi-artist tracks, an explicit track and accented names. Its description has HTML-escaped quotes (`&quot;`).
- Other playlist names include Arabic (`أغاني مستقلة`) and a leading `=` (`=1+1 Formula Test`). Some names returned by Spotify have trailing spaces.
- `/albums?ids=` returns `null` for a show ID and `/audio-features?ids=` returns `null` for an episode ID (see the batches noted in `live/index.json`).
- Response `href`s echo the browser's `locale` query parameter.

## Not covered

No playlist is `collaborative: true`, the playlist list and Liked Songs each fit in a single page, and there are no local files. Build those with fixture builders.
